description: The plot illustrates the ratio of loss values of different methods to that of Vanilla with respect to FLOPs. The x-axis is labeled "FLOPs" and has a logarithmic scale, ranging from approximately 1e+19 to 1e+21, with tick labels at regular intervals. The y-axis is labeled "Loss Ratio" and has a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 0.8, with tick labels at intervals of 0.1. The plot contains five lines, each representing a different method: Vanilla (blue, solid line, circle markers), StrmLLM (n=64) (orange, solid line, triangle markers), SepLLM (n=64) (green, solid line, square markers), SepLLM (n=64, H) (red, dashed line, diamond markers), and SepLLM (n=64, H/T) (purple, dashed line, cross markers). The lines generally decrease as FLOPs increase, with the Vanilla line remaining at a ratio of 1. The other lines start at higher ratios, around 1.6-1.8, and decrease to around 0.2-0.4 at the highest FLOPs value. Specifically, StrmLLM (n=64) starts at around 1.7 and ends at around 0.25, SepLLM (n=64) starts at around 1.6 and ends at around 0.25, SepLLM (n=64, H) starts at around 1.7 and ends at around 0.3, and SepLLM (n=64, H/T) starts at around 1.8 and ends at around 0.35.
